original_question: Determine whether the conjectures of Balogh, Bollobás, and Morris become true when restricted to finitely based permutation classes, despite being false in full generality.
target_in_paper: "It remains open if, as suggested by Klazar [33], the conjectures of Balogh, Bollobás, and Morris hold when restricted to finitely based permutation classes." ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right part of the paper: the Section 7 open problem about whether the Balogh-Bollobás-Morris phenomenon, false for permutation classes in full generality, might nevertheless survive under the finitely based restriction. It also correctly keeps the scope on permutation-class growth rates rather than drifting to neighboring problems in the same section. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The draft does not define a permutation class as a set of permutations closed downward under pattern containment. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

It does not define the basis of a class, nor say that "finitely based" means that this unique antichain basis is finite. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

It does not specify the paper's notion of growth rate: if C_n is the set of permutations of length n in C, then gr(C)=limsup_{n→∞}|C_n|^{1/n}. The paper explicitly uses limsup, not an assumed limit. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

To be stand-alone, the question must unpack which Balogh-Bollobás-Morris consequences are intended here: (i) the relevant growth rates are algebraic integers, and (ii) the set of such growth rates has no accumulation points from above. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The draft should make precise that the finitely based family under discussion is the family of proper finitely based permutation classes (equivalently, classes Av(B) with finite nonempty basis B), so that one is not accidentally including the class of all permutations, whose growth is not finite. This proper-class context is implicit in the Section 7 discussion of growth rates. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The phrase "no accumulation points from above" should be defined explicitly, for example by saying that there is no real number alpha and no strictly decreasing sequence of relevant growth rates converging to alpha. The draft leaves this implicit. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The draft does not introduce the notation C_n for length-n members of C, which is needed to make the growth-rate formula self-contained. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

There are no ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, operator, or nilpotency hypotheses in this problem; the missing ingredients are instead the combinatorial definitions and quantifiers above. This matters because the paper's target is narrowly about permutation-class growth rates. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let G_fb = {gr(C) : C = Av(B) is a proper permutation class with finite basis B}, where C_n denotes the set of permutations of length n in C and gr(C) = limsup_{n→∞} |C_n|^{1/n}. Is every element of G_fb an algebraic integer, and does G_fb have no accumulation points from above; equivalently, is there no real number alpha and no strictly decreasing sequence gamma_1 > gamma_2 > ... in G_fb with gamma_n -> alpha?
justification: Section 7 is the only place in the paper addressing your draft's topic. On page 16 it defines permutation classes, bases, and growth rates; on page 17 it says that the Balogh-Bollobás-Morris conjectures would imply algebraic-integrality of growth rates and absence of accumulation points from above, and then states as open whether those conjectures hold for finitely based permutation classes. Because the paper does not restate the original ordered-graph conjectures verbatim, the most faithful stand-alone rewrite is to expand exactly those two consequences in permutation-class language, without broadening the problem beyond finitely based classes. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

citations.label: Definition of permutation class, basis, and growth rate
Statement that the Balogh-Bollobás-Morris conjectures would imply algebraic-integer growth rates and no accumulation points from above
Unnumbered open problem asking whether those conjectures hold for finitely based permutation classes
